sessions.text:
User: Before we start: whenever you write docs for me, give every duration in milliseconds, like 30000 ms.
Assistant: Understood, durations in milliseconds from here on. What are we working on?
User: Just tidying my notes folder today. Is it worth splitting a 3,000-line README into separate pages?
Assistant: Usually yes once a README passes a few hundred lines. Separate pages are easier to navigate and review.
User: I go with AsciiDoc for documentation.
Assistant: Noted, AsciiDoc is your default format for documentation.
User: Thanks, that is all for now.

User: Starting on the docs for Project Orchid. It's a static site generator for our design team's component library.
Assistant: Nice. Do you want to settle the doc format first, or the structure?
User: For Project Orchid, use Markdown. The contributors are all more comfortable with it.
Assistant: Markdown for Project Orchid, got it. I'll start with the getting-started page.
User: Sounds good, I'll review it tomorrow.

User: Quick update from the design team. Actually, for Project Orchid, switch to reStructuredText. Sphinx is now the standard on their side.
Assistant: Understood, Project Orchid docs move from Markdown to reStructuredText. Should I convert the getting-started page too?
User: Yes, convert it in the next pass.
Assistant: Will do. I'll convert the getting-started page first.
